title: Grade 4 Math — Fri, May 29
description: Perimeter & Area — Day 5 of 5: Synthesis — real-world problems
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Perimeter formula for a rectangle with length l and width w?
Area formula for a rectangle?
questions.explanation: Area = length × width (l × w). Measured in square units.

questions.question: Farmer Ram has 60 m of fencing. He wants to make a rectangle as large as possible. Best dimensions?
questions.explanation: Fixed perimeter (60 m): a square maximises area. Side = 60÷4 = 15 m. Area = 15×15 = 225 m² — largest possible.

questions.question: A path of width 2 m goes around a rectangular garden 18 m × 12 m. Area of the path?
Square room costs ₹80/m² to tile and ₹60/m to skirting-board. Room side = 5 m. Total cost?
Two plots: A is 30×20 m, B is 25×24 m. Which has bigger area? Which needs more fencing?
options: A bigger area; A more fencing
B bigger area; A more fencing
B bigger area; B more fencing
questions.explanation: A = 30×20 = 600 m². B = 25×24 = 600 m². Same area! P(A) = 2×50 = 100 m, P(B) = 2×49 = 98 m. A needs more fencing.

questions.question: Rectangle: length is 3 times the width. Perimeter = 48 cm. Find area.
School courtyard 40×30 m. 200 students stand at 1 m² each. Is there enough space?
options: No — courtyard is 1,200 m², need 200 m²
questions.explanation: Courtyard area = 40×30 = 1,200 m². 200 students × 1 m² = 200 m². Yes, plenty of space.

questions.question: A 5 m × 5 m room has a window 2 m × 1.5 m and a door 1 m × 2 m on one wall. Area of wall left for painting? (wall height = 3 m)
questions.explanation: Wall = 5×3=15 m². Window=2×1.5=3 m². Door=1×2=2 m². Paintable=15−3−2=10 m².

questions.question: New square courtyard needed with area 4 times the original 5×5 m square. New side length?
questions.explanation: Original area = 25 m². New area = 4×25 = 100 m². New side = √100 = 10 m.

questions.question: Summary: key difference between perimeter and area?
options: Perimeter = inside space; Area = outside edge
Perimeter = outside edge length (cm/m); Area = inside surface (cm²/m²)
Area is always bigger than perimeter
questions.explanation: Perimeter → distance around edge, measured in cm/m. Area → surface covered inside, measured in cm²/m².

questions.question: When area doubles, does perimeter also double?
options: No — they are independent. Example: 4×4 (A=16,P=16) vs 8×2 (A=16,P=20)
questions.explanation: Area and perimeter are independent. Same area can have very different perimeters and vice versa.

questions.question: Composite shape: 10×6 rectangle with a 4×4 square added on top of the middle. Total area?
questions.explanation: Rectangle = 10×6 = 60 cm². Square = 4×4 = 16 cm². Total = 60+16 = 76 cm².

questions.question: Ribbon around a 24 cm × 16 cm gift box (perimeter). Ribbon costs ₹5 per cm. Cost?
Best summary of this week's learning:
options: Area and perimeter are the same
Perimeter = total edge; Area = surface inside; same shape can have different P and A; composite shapes split into parts
Area is measured in cm, perimeter in cm²
questions.explanation: Week synthesis: Perimeter (edge, linear units) and Area (inside surface, square units) are distinct. Composite shapes break into rectangles. Fixed perimeter → square maximises area.
